title: The blessing to carry (Numbers 6:24–26)
hookLine: the Lord bless you and keep you, and give you peace
carry: the lord bless you and keep you
tomorrow: can you be excited and terrified about the same thing?

cards: Someone says your name across a loud room, and your head turns before you've decided to turn it. A name said warmly lands in the body. One blessing in the book of Numbers is built that way.
"The LORD bless thee, and keep thee." Listen to the small word. Thee.
In the King James, thee is one person. Not you all. You.
The priests stood before a whole people, and the words were shaped for each one of them.

teach.b: In Numbers, God tells Moses to tell Aaron and his sons, "On this wise ye shall bless the children of Israel."

Then the words: "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace." Feel what each line does.
Keep: guarded, watched over, the way shepherds keep a flock by night.
A face that shines: someone turning toward you with light in their face, glad you're there.
A countenance lifted up: being looked at, not past. And peace, the last gift, the one the whole blessing walks toward.

These were Israel's words first, and Jews pray them still; some churches speak them over people at the end of a service. Then the next verse: "they shall put my name upon the children of Israel; and I will bless them."
The priest speaks; God blesses. The one saying it passes it on, and never owns it. That's why the blessing can travel.

teach.h: THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU.
teach.b: A parent can say it over a sleeping child. A friend can say it beside a hospital bed. And a person can say it over themselves on the way out the door.

how: Jews pray the priestly blessing in the synagogue, and some churches close their services with it, the minister raising a hand or both hands over the people.

games.q: what does “the blessing to carry” mean?
o: a prayer said before meals in Israel's homes
a farewell speech Moses gave before he died
an old blessing from Numbers, said to one person

s: in the King James, 'thee' means one person
the blessing is spoken to a whole people, and worded for each one.
the blessing belongs only to churches
these were Israel's words first, and Jews pray them still.
the priest who speaks the blessing is its source
Numbers 6:27: they put God's name on the people, 'and I will bless them.'

games.q: a teacher closes graduation by saying Numbers 6 over the whole class. why is it worded "thee," not "you all"?
o: an old printing slip in the King James.
it was first written for a single king.
it's shaped for each person, one at a time.
games.why: spoken over a whole people, the blessing addresses each one: thee, singular. in a crowd, every person hears their own blessing.

practice: Say the blessing out loud over yourself, slowly, one line to a breath, and hear your own voice say thee. Then say it again with one person's name in it, as if they were sitting across from you.

wordCard.voice: The blessing to carry. Three lines from Numbers, worded for one person at a time: bless and keep, shine and be gracious, lift up and give peace.

orig.note: Hebrew: may he bless you (one person). the first word of the blessing in Numbers 6:24.

carryVoice: Your line: the lord bless you and keep you. The priests spoke it, and passed it on. Peace to you.
